Revised assessment incorporating SLOOS: The statement’s nod to “strong fundamentals” is outweighed by an intermeeting 50 bp cut and expanded liquidity operations, which already signal risk management mode. SLOOS readings around this time point to tightening credit supply and weaker risk appetite: banks tightened C&I and construction/land development standards, raised credit score thresholds and cut limits, reported weaker demand in certain loan categories, and expected tighter standards on riskier loans along with deterioration in collateral values and loan performance in 2020. These survey signals imply additional headwinds to activity and funding beyond the noted money market pressures, making the overall tone more defensive and precautionary than the text alone suggests.
